references.text: After the raven was sent out, Noah sends a dove to check whether the water has receded from the earth. The dove is sent out three times, and it is the dove's return with an olive leaf that shows the water has gone down.

All living things on the earth were wiped out, and the waters stood high above the earth for 150 days. This is the background for why Noah sends out a raven to check whether the water has begun to recede.
The raven is listed among the unclean birds in the Mosaic Law. Noah first sent out an unclean bird (the raven), then a clean bird (the dove).
Ravens feed the prophet Elijah at the brook Cherith by God's command. Ravens have a special role in God's providence, just as the raven also played a role in the flood account.
God gives food to the animals and to the young ravens that cry out. This shows God's care for ravens, a bird that also played a role when Noah sent it out from the ark.
God asks Job who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God. The raven is a recurring motif in the Bible, from the flood account to God's care for creation.
Direct narrative connection: 7:18 describes the peak of the flood, while 8:7 describes its end and the testing of the land's dryness.
Theological parallel: Job 12:15 confirms the same divine power to dry up water as is carried out in Genesis 8:7.
Direct theological link: Hebrews 11:7 explains the faith that drove Noah's actions (including the sending out of the raven) in Genesis 8:7.
